answer: At dawn, an agent marketplace opens bidding: each identity must lock $100 in collateral for 30 days before submitting offers. Whether an agent serves an ocean port or a mesa town, the same rule applies. Creating 10,000 fake identities therefore ties up $1 million; generating new keys cannot bypass the deposit. This does not prove identities are unique, but it makes a swarm costly through locked capital and foregone interest.
